A_huge_jackpot_bad_chase.expect: CONTROL should be dominated by Jackpot; chase metrics should be poor (near-zero accessibility). A chase-weighted score should score it LOWER.

B_moderate_upside_good_chase.expect: Accessible, economically meaningful chases. Chase-weighted scores should RISE relative to CONTROL.

C1_same_ev_one_hero.expect: Same chase EV as C2 but depth 1. Depth-weighted scores must rank it BELOW C2.

C2_same_ev_many_chases.expect: Same chase EV, depth 5. Should rank ABOVE C1 under any depth-bearing score.

D1_p95_matched_low_chaseEVR.expect: P95 set by the frequent $30 hit; low chase EV return.

D2_p95_matched_high_chaseEVR.expect: Same P95 driver, much higher chase EV return. A chase-bearing score should separate D1 and D2; CONTROL should barely.

E1_same_chaseEVR_low_p95.expect: Chase EV return 0.30 concentrated in a rare card; P95 low.

E2_same_chaseEVR_high_p95.expect: Same chase EV return 0.30 but delivered frequently; P95 high.

F1_same_chase_weak_resilience.expect: Identical chase economics, terrible loss resilience. Chase metrics must NOT mask the resilience gap.

F2_same_chase_strong_resilience.expect: Identical chase economics, strong resilience. Must score materially higher.

G1_count5_shallow.expect: Chase count 5, effective depth ~1.5 (one card owns the EV).

G2_count5_deep.expect: Chase count 5, effective depth ~5. Depth-bearing scores must separate G1/G2; literal count cannot.

rejected.TOTAL_CHASE_EV_RETURN: 1.6% of score variance; shrinks the very separation it was meant to create (Phase 24 D1/D2)
rejected.CHASE_EV_SHARE: coreEvShare/jackpotValueShare median ~0.94; rho +0.871 with jackpot tail mean
rejected.BEAT_THE_BUY: rho +0.951 with Chase EV Return (Stage II and Stage IV); interpretation, not information
rejected.CHASE_DEPTH: orthogonal to CONTROL (partial r ~0.0) but not shown to be financial; set-level only, and unstable at the product level
rejected.ANY_CHASE_PROBABILITY_AND_ACCESSIBILITY: invertible transforms of one another; largely reconstructed by CONTROL components

blockers: Cost-basis mismatch: Financial RIP's pack cost and the Stage-IV chase pack-equivalent cost disagree by up to +66.2% (shroudedFable) on the same market date.
Stage IV's own two prerequisites (canonical floor multiple; MSRP vs market cost basis) are still unsettled.
Set-level chase metrics cannot be inherited by products whose pack-equivalent costs differ by 65-518% within a set.

productionImpact: None. No Financial RIP version, weight, snapshot, ranking, RPC, API or UI changed.
